verdicts.reason: Kind: fact. S1 says DBS, OCBC and UOB 'have successfully completed live domestic Singapore dollar transactions using tokenised deposits on Swift's blockchain-based ledger.' It calls this the first time the three banks have executed live interbank transactions using tokenised deposits, and describes it as a collaboration. That matches the claim.

Kind: fact. S1 is a press release dated 'Singapore, 10 September 2026', and it says the banks 'have successfully completed' the transactions. That shows they were done by 10 Sep, but it never gives the date they were actually carried out. Treating the announcement date as the transaction date says more than the source does.

Kind: absence. No source describes one member acting alone in a way that peers are expected to follow. S1 describes a joint three-bank move. S2 covers a Fed rate hike that affects all three banks. S3 is a Jefferies coverage initiation. One caveat: S1 quotes UOB calling itself the first Singapore-headquartered bank to complete live transactions on Swift's ledger. That is first-mover wording, but no source presents it as a move peers are likely to follow, so it does not clearly contradict the claim. The claim's 'must follow' is also stronger than the question's 'likely to follow', but an absence claim only fails when a source contradicts it, and none does.
